rationale: The defining cohort study of Karayol-Borroto-Haghshenas neurodevelopmental syndrome (Karayol et al., 2024; OMIM #620985) delineating 25 individuals with heterozygous de novo MSL2 variants demonstrates that motor dysfunction is prominent in almost all affected individuals (motor delay in 21/25, accompanied by hypotonia, gait disturbance, coordination difficulties, and feeding problems). Conversely, seizures occur in a minority (9/25, ~36%) and are characterized as occurring 'to a lesser extent' rather than presenting as severe early intractable epileptic encephalopathy or progressive spasticity, thereby supporting the phenotypic distinction of MSL2-related neurodevelopmental disorder from other severe MSL/NSL complex disorders.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 25 individuals with heterozygous de novo MSL2 variants, clinical presentation featured global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and motor issues including coordination problems, feeding difficulties, and gait disturbance, whereas seizures occurred to a lesser extent.

new_directions.question_text: What is the detailed semiology, age of onset, and drug-responsiveness of seizures in the subset of MSL2 patients who develop epilepsy compared to KAT8/MSL3 cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Although only 9 of 25 patients exhibited seizures, precise electroclinical phenotyping will determine whether MSL2 seizures represent benign/focal events or can evolve into epileptic encephalopathy under specific genetic modifiers.

new_directions.question_text: Does the severity of coordination deficit and cerebellar-like gait ataxia correlate with specific MSL2 protein domains (e.g., RING vs CXC/coiled-coil domains) or episignature intensity?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying domain-specific genotype-phenotype correlations could explain why motor coordination problems and hypotonia predominate over spasticity in this syndrome.
